MATCHED-ARM EXPERIMENT - the decisive design for this epic. Both arms estimate Sigma from exactly FOUR runs, differing only in whether the two evaluated runs are among them. Anything surviving is provenance; anything that vanishes was data volume.

  disjoint : the 4 runs excluding {a,b}     (no evaluation residuals)
  overlap  : {a,b} + 2 others               (includes evaluation residuals)

R=6, reps=500, shrinkage=0.05, n=48, p=12, base R, no package code, seed 20260813.

  NULL (target 0.000000)
    disjoint  mean -0.000251  var 4.076e-05  RMSE 0.006383  MCse 0.000286
    overlap   mean -0.000061  var 4.354e-05  RMSE 0.006592  MCse 0.000295
    paired    mean +0.000190  MCse 0.000079  z +2.40  90% CI [+0.000060, +0.000320]

  SIGNAL (target 0.020462)
    disjoint  mean +0.020470  bias +0.000008  var 1.531e-04  RMSE 0.012362  MCse 0.000553
    overlap   mean +0.020628  bias +0.000166  var 1.545e-04  RMSE 0.012419  MCse 0.000556
    paired    mean +0.000158  MCse 0.000114  z +1.39  90% CI [-0.000029, +0.000345]

THE HEADLINE: the large unmatched effect is a CONFOUND, and it disappears.

  unmatched signal paired diff  -0.002028   z -9.81
  matched   signal paired diff  +0.000158   z +1.39

A 13x reduction and a sign flip. So the z = -9.81 I reported last pass was data volume - 2 training runs versus 4 - not evaluation-residual contamination. Confirms the mechanism I proposed, and it is the concrete instance of your criterion 5, evaluator correctness versus learner quality: the evaluator is fine, the learner was being starved.

Note also the matched disjoint SIGNAL bias is +0.000008 against a target of 0.020462 - essentially unbiased. The estimator is correct; the earlier apparent bias was entirely an artefact of how much data the metric got.

WHAT REMAINS, stated with appropriate caution. On the NULL arm the matched difference is +0.000190 with z = +2.40 and a 90% CI excluding zero. That is a small residual provenance effect: about 0.9% of the signal target and about 3% of per-realization RMSE. I would NOT call it established - it is one seed, 500 replications, and it is one of two arms tested, so at z = 2.40 it is marginal. It needs replication at higher reps or across seeds before it should appear in a report as a real effect.

RECOMMENDED CONCLUSION FOR THE EPIC

1. Report the matched design as the primary comparison; the unmatched one is confounded by training-set size and should not be the headline.
2. State the equivalence margin from the matched arms. At 500 reps here the 90% CIs bound any provenance effect to roughly +/-0.0003, i.e. under 1.5% of a typical signal magnitude.
3. Record the small null-arm z = +2.40 as a follow-up research question, not a finding - which is exactly what your last acceptance criterion asks for.
4. Keep the shrinkage level explicit; I only tested lambda = 0.05 in the matched design, and the unmatched sweep showed the volume effect shrinks as lambda rises, so the matched result may be lambda-dependent too.
